prior_dispositions_note: P1-P8 and N1-N10 were NOT reopened or rewritten. The only edits outside P9/P10/P11 are minimal cross-references directly coupled to them: the 'bootstrap' meaning of classifyPdfError/PdfFallbackReason (spec facade row, task .2, task .4) and the P-4a/P-4b cancellation cross-reference (task .3, task .4).

P9.finding: The P-4 protocol was internally impossible: samples waited for the previous render to settle, yet cancel-before-restart was required on every commit, so a correct renderer could fail.
P9.resolution: P-4 is now two independent checks that are never conflated. P-4a (sequential re-render latency): 20 alternating 100%/200% commits on the small fixture at fit-width, each commit issued only after the previous visible render settled; sample = commit -> last visible renderSettle(completed); ascending sort; p95 = 19th of 20; threshold <= 500 ms; no renderCancel is required or expected and its absence is explicitly not a failure; the only ordering assertion is that every renderStart reaches a terminal renderSettle. P-4b (deliberately overlapping cancellation ordering): commit a zoom/fit change, prove the render is in flight by polling __gnoPdfMetrics until that generation has a renderStart with no terminal settle (escalate render cost - larger fixture, higher zoom, larger viewport - if it always settles too fast; fail loudly if in-flight state can never be observed; never fall back to a sleep or skip), then issue the replacement commit while in flight and assert on the recorded event stream that the superseded generation's renderCancel precedes its renderSettle(cancelled) and both precede the replacement generation's first renderStart, that the superseded generation never later records renderSettle(completed), and that no stale output is painted; run at least twice (zoom->zoom and zoom->fit-mode) with the full ordered event stream stored in the evidence artifact. Task .3 additionally forbids synthesizing a renderCancel for an already-terminal task.

P10.finding: The plan assumed cMap/standard-font 404s produce the same classified document-load bootstrap failure as a worker failure, making the required cMap/font fallback screenshots and notices unreachable through the specified architecture.
P10.resolution: All claims that auxiliary-asset 404s necessarily reject the document load or enter DocView's bootstrap fallback are removed. Worker startup/bootstrap failure (404-fulfilled worker route) remains the sole deterministic bootstrap reason/notice/fallback UI case and the only bootstrap sub-case in task .6's R8 state list; R8 states this exclusion explicitly. The failure-mode table now carries a separate auxiliary-asset row stating observed PDF.js semantics: missing cMap/standard-font data typically surfaces as a warning and/or degraded glyph/text output and may in some cases produce a page-render error, so no document-load fallback transition is required. Task .6 defines two executable auxiliary-asset checks (404-fulfilled cMap request while opening cjk-cmap.pdf; 404-fulfilled standard-font request while opening standard-font.pdf) asserting: the expected same-origin request was attempted and fulfilled 404; the outcome PDF.js genuinely produces is captured first and then asserted against that capture - console warning text via a Playwright console listener dumped verbatim, and/or degraded text-layer content plus canvas pixel sample diffed against the same fixture in the clean run, or a classified page-render error if one is genuinely produced; zero non-self requests (no external/CDN/file: fallback); security envelope unchanged (CSP without unsafe-eval, frame-ancestors 'none', X-Frame-Options DENY); the viewer stays actionable (toolbar, Pages/Text toggle, download) and never crashes; determinism proven by running each case twice with identical classification, raw observations stored in the evidence artifact. No bootstrap classification, fallback transition, or DocView notice is required or asserted for these cases. No page-error propagation architecture is invented: if the observed outcome turns out to be a genuine page-render error the current architecture cannot surface, task .6 reports it as a finding for the spec owner. R18 records the auxiliary cases separately from the R8 state list. The meaning of 'bootstrap' is pinned at the classifier definition sites (spec facade row, task .2) and at the consumer (task .4) as a worker-startup/document-load rejection only.

P11.resolution: Spec JSON branch_name set to exactly feat/native-pdf-renderer.
